title: What If a Magnetar Flared Near Earth? One Already Did

scenes.text: What if a magnetar flared near Earth? One already did, from the far side of the galaxy.
On December 27, 2004, a burst from a magnetar called SGR 1806-20 reached us after crossing about 50,000 light-years.
In a tenth of a second, it released more energy than the Sun gives off in 100,000 years.
It heated Earth's upper atmosphere and made it expand. Amateur radio watchers saw their signal jump.
At that distance, even an astronaut facing the full blast would have taken less radiation than a dental X-ray.
Bring it closer than about six light-years, and a University of Kansas estimate says a flare like that could seriously damage our atmosphere.
